template.tagline: Dense fuel down low, hydrogen up high.
template.brief: A kerosene first stage does the heavy lifting through the thick air, where dense propellant keeps tanks small. Above it, a wide, light hydrogen stage with two expander engines uses its high specific impulse (about 465 s) to push a 4 t satellite toward geostationary transfer orbit.

benchmark.class: Kerolox or solid booster with a hydrogen upper stage
benchmark.text: Hydrogen/oxygen upper stages have flown since the 1960s because their efficiency pays off most where every kilogram of stage mass must be pushed to orbital speed. Their low density makes tanks large, which is why they are rarely used alone on first stages.
